Reena: guess who got picked to captain the inter-school debate 🎉
Yusuf: obviously you. congrats!!
Reena: also Mrs Pillai asked if I can keep tutoring her twins Tues and Thurs, and I said yes
Yusuf: with boards AND coaching?? when do you sleep
Reena: sleep is for after March 😎 did physics till 1:30 last night and still woke up at 6
Yusuf: that's kind of wild
Reena: coaching sir said I'm the only one in the batch who never misses homework. and Papa told Chachi I'm the reliable one
Yusuf: you are. just saying you don't have to be everything
Reena: but I LIKE it. I feel unstoppable rn
Yusuf: ok unstoppable, can you prep with me for the mock on Sat then?
Reena: yes of course!! 💪
Yusuf: you just added another thing
Reena: it's fine, I'll fit it in

qa.q: Until what time did Reena do physics the night before?
qa.a: Till 1:30, and Reena still woke up at 6.

qa.q: What does 'I feel unstoppable rn' suggest about how the busy schedule feels to Reena right now?
qa.a: It feels exciting and makes Reena proud 😊; praise from coaching sir and Papa seems to fuel the pace.

qa.q: What small turning point is available to Reena at this stage?
qa.a: Before saying yes again, Reena could fix a sleep time and drop or delay one commitment, such as the tutoring, while energy is still high.

qa.q: How does Yusuf see Reena's growing list?
qa.a: Yusuf is impressed but uneasy about the lost sleep, and notices out loud when one more thing gets added, even Yusuf's own request.

grounding: Shows a teenage high-achiever piling on commitments with pride, cutting sleep while praise keeps the pace going.

passage:
By six in the morning Aparna was already on the local bus to Sangamner, flashcards in one hand, a steel dabba in the other. Coaching till nine, school till four, then debate practice in the empty Marathi classroom, where Joshi Sir clapped and said, "Our taluka champion!"
Evenings she sat at Baba's kirana counter, totalling bills faster than the calculator, while customers told Baba, "Such a clever girl you have." She glowed every time.
At midnight her little brother Akash found her still at the counter, chemistry book open under the single shop bulb.
"Tai, Aai said go to sleep."
"Five more pages," she said, grinning. "I'm not even tired, Akash. I could do this forever."
He watched her yawn right through the sentence, then went to bed alone.

qa.q: What did Joshi Sir call Aparna at debate practice?
qa.a: "Our taluka champion!"

qa.q: How did Aparna feel when customers praised her, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She felt proud; the passage says she glowed every time they called her clever.

qa.q: How could Aai or Baba step in at this stage?
qa.a: They could notice the midnight studying and help Aparna set a sleep time or step back from the shop counter during exam months, while praising rest as well as work.

qa.q: What does Akash notice that Aparna doesn't?
qa.a: Akash sees his Tai yawn right through saying she isn't tired, and he ends up going to bed alone.

grounding: Illustrates a teen taking on coaching, debate, exams and shop work with pride and high energy, while sleep shrinks and praise fuels the pace.

passage:
The school noticeboard had Zubin's name on three lists: debate captain, science exhibition lead, and peer tutor for Class 8. Swati ma'am stopped him in the corridor.
"Zubin! The principal says you've also taken the quiz team? With boards in four months?"
"I can manage, ma'am." He grinned. "I sleep five hours. It's enough."
"You're the most reliable student I have."
Zubin felt a glow all the way to the lab. After coaching he'd tutor two juniors, then prepare his debate notes till one.
He didn't mention the part-time job at his uncle's shop on Saturdays. He liked being the one everyone could count on.

qa.q: How many hours does Zubin say he sleeps?
qa.a: Five hours.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when Swati ma'am called him reliable?
qa.a: He felt proud and energised, glowing with praise that pushed him to take on even more.

qa.q: What turning point could help Zubin at this early stage?
qa.a: Pausing to drop one commitment and protecting his sleep, perhaps with Swati ma'am's help, before the pace wears him down.

qa.q: What might Swati ma'am be thinking as she praises him?
qa.a: She seems impressed but slightly concerned, since she asks about boards in four months.

grounding: Shows a high-achieving teen piling on commitments, proud to be reliable, sleeping less and fuelled by praise.

passage:
Dear Parul didi,
Guess what! I got selected for the state debate, AND I'm still doing the science olympiad, AND coaching, AND I'm helping Mumma with her tiffin orders in the evenings. Oh, and boards, of course.
Everyone keeps saying, "Ritu, how do you do it all?" Honestly, I love hearing that. I'm the one who never drops anything. My class teacher says I'm the most dependable girl in school.
I've been sleeping from 1 to 6. It's fine! I feel so alive. I've made a colour-coded timetable with fifteen-minute slots.
When you visit in December, I'll show you my trophy shelf.
Love,
Ritu

qa.q: What hours has Ritu been sleeping?
qa.a: From 1 to 6.

qa.q: What is Ritu feeling as she lists everything?
qa.a: She feels excited and proud, enjoying being the dependable one who never drops anything.

qa.q: What could Parul didi gently suggest at this stage?
qa.a: That Ritu protect her sleep and choose which one or two things matter most, before the pace catches up with her.

qa.q: How might Parul didi feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Parul didi may feel proud of Ritu but worried about the late nights and packed timetable.

grounding: Shows a high-achieving teen proudly taking on debate, olympiad, coaching, helping at home and boards, cutting sleep, fuelled by praise.

passage:
Okay, Rukmini, you want my schedule? Listen. Six a.m., school. Four p.m., coaching. Seven, debate practice. Nine, I teach my neighbour's kids maths, they pay me a little. Eleven till one, board revision.
Yes, I know. But honestly? I love it. Everyone says, "Ask Ayesha, she'll do it." The principal called me a role model in assembly. Do you know how that feels?
Sleep? I'll sleep after boards. Right now I feel like I could run a marathon.
You're laughing, but you'll see. I'm going to do all of it, and do it well. That's who I am, the girl who never says no.

qa.q: What does Ayesha do at nine?
qa.a: Ayesha teaches the neighbour's kids maths.

qa.q: What is Ayesha feeling while describing the schedule?
qa.a: She feels excited and proud, energised by praise and being the girl who never says no.

qa.q: What turning point could help Ayesha before it's too late?
qa.a: Learning that saying no to one thing and sleeping properly is not failing, perhaps with a parent or teacher helping Ayesha choose.

qa.q: How might Rukmini be seeing Ayesha's plan?
qa.a: Rukmini seems amused but perhaps worried, laughing at a pace that leaves no time for sleep.

grounding: Shows a teen proud of taking on school, coaching, debate and tutoring, cutting sleep and driven by praise.

passage:
Monday, June. After class, Ms Elizabeth asked who would lead the debate team this year. Lalremsiami's hand was up before she had finished. "I knew I could count on you," the teacher said, and the words glowed in her chest all the way home through the Aizawl drizzle.
Saturday, two weeks later. Board exam coaching three evenings a week, debate practice on two, and now she had said yes to tutoring the neighbour's twins on Sundays. She coloured her timetable with five highlighters and taped it above her desk. Lights out after one, alarm at five. She felt unstoppable.
Friday, July. Her team won the inter-school debate. In assembly the principal called her "the most reliable student in Class 12". Back home she added two more items to her list and hid a long yawn from her mother.

qa.q: How many highlighters did Lalremsiami use for her timetable?
qa.a: Five highlighters.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling when the teacher said "I knew I could count on you"?
qa.a: She felt proud and energised; the praise glowed in her chest all the way home.

qa.q: What turning point is available at this stage?
qa.a: An adult could notice the late nights and praise rest and limits, not only results, and help her drop one commitment.

qa.q: How might Ms Elizabeth see Lalremsiami right now?
qa.a: She likely sees a proud, capable student and may not notice the lost sleep behind the results.

grounding: Shows a high-achieving teen saying yes to exams, coaching, debate and tutoring, cutting sleep while praise keeps her going.
